references.text: Aaron placed the testimony (the tablets of the law) in the ark, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
God gave Moses the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets written with God's finger.
Moses came down from the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand, tablets that were written on both sides.
Moses took the testimony and put it in the ark, set the poles on the ark, and placed the mercy seat above the ark.
God said he would write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, and Moses was to place them in the ark.
Moses placed the tablets in the ark he had made, just as the Lord had commanded him.
There was nothing else in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb.
The ark of the covenant contained a golden jar of manna, Aaron's staff that had budded, and the tablets of the covenant.
This is a direct fulfillment of the instruction in the source verse; 40:3 shows the actual action where the testimony was placed into the ark.
The verse uses the definition from the source verse ('ark of the testimony') to establish the altar's placement in relation to God's presence.
Verse 22 explains the theological consequence of the content in verse 16: God's presence and speech are linked to the covenant's testimony.
The verses describe two necessary and complementary parts of the same unit: the contents of the ark and the cover that shields them.
Both verses establish that holy acts must take place in direct relation to God's word ('before the testimony').
